non_claims: acetate versus methyl ester is not resolved by the C2H4O2 loss
the vindoline (aspidosperma) skeleton is not claimed; C12H14NO+ is also printed for other methoxyindole alkaloids
the methoxy position is not resolved
a C2H4O2 difference also arises from two sequential losses (CH3OH then CO, or ketene then H2O), so the loss alone does not show an acetate or methyl ester

notes: measure:false, provisional (WS0 2026-11-19) pending the author: the P3 proposal makes every monoterpene indole alkaloid rule report-only, so this rule is kept but not measured.

competitors.note: N-acyl aspidospermanes without an ester in the shared list (aspidocarpine, PubChem 632854; aspidolimine, 579958) can reach the C2H4O2 difference by ketene then H2O loss (not checked against a source).

Methyl ethers without an acetate or methyl ester (for example the aryl methoxy aspidospermanes of the shared list) can reach the C2H4O2 difference by CH3OH then CO loss (not checked against a source).
